videos.title: Riverine sand and gravel mining, northeast Bangladesh
videos.text: From hand-dug pits on the sand bars to boat fleets, suction-pump dredging, sieving towers, truck queues and sand-filled land: the supply chain the atlas traces from space.
videos.credit: Shown in the AGU 2025 talk (Chyon, Best and Haq)

videos.title: Someshwari River sand mining, January 2024
videos.text: Rows of floating suction-pump pipelines span the channel while the sand bars are excavated, the reach the atlas dates to 2021 to 2025.
videos.credit: Drone footage: M. S. A. Chyon

videos.title: Gravel mining pits at Lubhachorra
videos.text: Water-filled gravel pits and spoil ridges on the floodplain and abandoned channels beside the Lubha, the pit field that converts in the atlas from 2012.
videos.credit: Drone footage: M. S. A. Chyon

videos.title: Lubha River, 2010 to 2023
videos.text: One RapidEye or PlanetScope scene a year: the pit field spreads across the floodplain and abandoned channels.

videos.title: Lubha River at 50 cm: SkySat, 2018 to 2023
videos.text: High-resolution SkySat scenes resolve individual pits and pit lakes along the channel.

videos.title: Channel pits on the Lubha, mapped year by year
videos.text: Pits mapped from high-resolution imagery: blue up to 300 m², red larger. Many more small pits than large ones point to artisanal digging.

videos.title: How sand mining is reshaping the Someshwari
videos.text: Gauges, wells, cross-sections and imagery bracket the 6.5 km mined reach: bed lowering, falling low-flow stage and the dredge fleet behind them.
videos.credit: Chyon and Best, Water Resources Research (in review), Video S1

videos.title: Where the sand goes: sand-filled land around Dhaka, 2001 to 2020
videos.text: Wetlands and paddy around the capital filled with river sand for housing and industry, the demand at the end of the chain.
